title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Strong axial crystal fields from bulky, electron-rich ligands, together with removal or rigidification of equatorial donors, suppress zero-field quantum tunneling and lengthen magnetic relaxation in Dy(III) single-molecule magnets.
explanation: Bulky electron-donating ligands build an axial field at Dy3+, and removing lateral chloride removes transverse interference with the magnetic axis. In a related dimer, terminal aminopyridine hydrogen bonds and π–π contacts stabilize a linear μ-Cl bridge, axial alkoxides increase anisotropy, and the H-bond network forces collinear Dy axes.
scope: Dy(III) mononuclear and binuclear SMMs with axial oxygen donors and controlled equatorial ligands.
conditions: Absence of laterally coordinated chloride in the bis(amide) case; hydrogen-bond and π–π stabilization of a linear μ-Cl bridge with axial alkoxides in the aminopyridine dimer.
caveats: Barrier heights and hysteresis temperatures are not restated numerically in the review.
